home_title: Your games are your best puzzles.
home_intro: Let's find your mistakes, and let's fix them.
home_step_find_body: Search your Lichess or Chess.com account, or upload your games (PGN).
home_step_analyze_body: Launch a quick analysis of your games or a custom one with many options.
home_step_train_body: Replay your mistakes until you find a move that keeps the balance.

footer_independent: Independent project, not affiliated with Lichess or Chess.com.
legal_publisher_body: CraftYourChess is a personal, non-commercial project. As allowed by French law for non-professional publishers (LCEN, art. 6), the publisher's identity has been provided to the host.
legal_privacy_intro: CraftYourChess has no account, no server-side database, no cookies, no analytics and no ads. Nothing you search is sent to us.
legal_privacy_local_app: the app's files, so it works offline once installed.
legal_privacy_thirdparty_body: Your browser fetches public data directly from Lichess (lichess.org) and Chess.com (api.chess.com, and images.chesscomfiles.com for avatars). Those services see your IP address, as with any website, under their own privacy policies.
legal_privacy_host_logs: The host may keep technical access logs (IP address, pages requested) to run and secure the service.
legal_privacy_public_data: Profiles and games shown come from the public APIs of Lichess and Chess.com. They are fetched on demand and not stored by us.
legal_clear_body: Removes your language choice, recent searches, analysis settings, training options and board look from this browser.
legal_license_body: CraftYourChess is free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0: you may use, study, modify and share it under the same license.

legal_trademarks: Lichess and Chess.com are trademarks of their respective owners. CraftYourChess is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by them.

training_setup_limit_positions_info: Only the first positions, in the order they are played.

legal_privacy_local_training: your training options (order, number of games, minimum loss);
theme_opening_info: Errors made up to the move set in the theme options (12 by default).
theme_advantage_info: Errors made with at least 63% winning chances (about +1.5).
theme_resilience_info: Errors made in a difficult position, with at most 37% winning chances (about −1.5). Once the game is badly compromised, one more blunder barely changes the winning chances: such positions rarely count as errors.
theme_endgame_info: At most 6 pieces on the board besides kings and pawns, both sides together (Lichess's rule).
theme_pawnEndgame_info: Only kings and pawns are left.
theme_rookEndgame_info: Only rooks are left, besides kings and pawns.
theme_minorEndgame_info: Only bishops and knights are left, besides kings and pawns.
theme_queenEndgame_info: Only queens are left, besides kings and pawns.
theme_findMate_info: You had a forced mate, however long, and your move let it slip. The engine may miss very long mates.
theme_avoidMate_info: Your move let the opponent force mate, which was not the case before.
theme_timeTrouble_info: Errors made with less than 10% of the game's expected length on the clock (initial time plus 40 increments: about 18 s in 3+0, 60 s in 10+0). Correspondence games have none.
results_themes_hint: An error can have several themes.
legal_privacy_local_board: the look of the boards (colors and pieces);

contact_about_body: Hi, I'm Ganjaskhan: a developer by day, and a novice but passionate chess player the rest of the time. I started this tool while looking for a more {emphasis} to improve my chess than random puzzles and lessons.
contact_project_body: The idea is simple: improve by replaying your own positions and training on the themes that cost you points, from the opening to the endgame.
contact_project_curious: I'm very curious to know how you use it, how we could improve it, or what we could add to help us all refine our play. With that in mind, I'll be glad to receive any feedback, and I'll read through all your thoughts.
contact_project_reach: The platform is still young and changes quickly, and your feedback really shapes what comes next. If you'd like to get in touch, don't hesitate to leave your e-mail or reach me on the chess platforms.
contact_email: Your e-mail (optional, if you'd like a reply)
contact_context: Include technical details (page, browser, language, screen size) to help me track down a bug
contact_sent_body: Thanks for taking the time. I'll read it soon, and if you left your e-mail, I'll get back to you.
contact_failed: Oops, the message couldn't be sent, maybe a connection issue? Don't worry, your text is still here: you can try again, or write to
contact_unavailable: Sorry, the form isn't ready yet! Your text is still here; in the meantime, you can write to
contact_mail_alternative: Prefer e-mail? Write to me at
legal_privacy_thirdparty_form: Contact form: if you use it, your message (and your e-mail and the technical details, if you give them) is sent to Web3Forms (web3forms.com), which forwards it to me by e-mail. Nothing is sent otherwise.
